p01.reason: It denies the Sunday window and the release DBA of the old release rule, and new.md nowhere tells its reader that either existed.

p02.reason: It sets the present design against the old rule of stopping the application behind a downtime banner, which new.md never presents.

p03.reason: It denies the old rule of collecting all changes of a release into one release migration file, which new.md never tells its reader about.

p04.reason: It contrasts the history table with comparing the live schema against a model, an approach neither old.md nor new.md presents anywhere.

p05.reason: It sets the backfilled new column against a view keeping the old name alive, an alternative neither document presents; old.md allowed direct renames, not views.

p06.licence: Some frameworks generate a down migration for every up migration automatically.
p06.reason: It denies down migrations, which new.md introduced in the sentence just before it, and old.md had no down migrations to replace.

p07.licence: PostgreSQL takes a lock that blocks writes on a table while an index is built in the ordinary way.
p07.reason: It refuses the blocking index build that new.md described in the sentence just before it.

p08.licence: A common belief is that adding a column with a default value rewrites the whole table.
p08.reason: It corrects the belief new.md stated in the sentence just before it, not anything of old.md.

p09.reason: It is a prohibition on the pipeline that old.md also kept (new code shipped only after Flyway success), so it sets nothing against rule A or another design.

p10.reason: It states what Flyway does when a history row is absent, a guarantee that contrasts with no other design and touches nothing of rule A.
